solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bribe gambler to accept help

indicators.note: to accept means the gambler's word takes the help word into its middle

parts.note: a backer is someone who bets on a horse or team
to give a hand is to help

explanation.surface: A punter takes on an assistant to cover his bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhander is slang for a secret payment slipped to someone to win a favour, a synonym for a bribe.

clue.text: A young man's responsibility

definitions.meaning: an old word for a dashing young fellow
the ... in 'the ... stops here' or 'pass the ...' is the duty to answer for something

explanation.definitionFit: Buck once meant a lively young man of fashion, and in the idiom about passing it, it means the burden of responsibility.

clue.text: Mistakenly credit rag for article in magazine

indicators.note: mistakenly says the letters of the two words are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A journal's credit has been wrongly given to a downmarket paper for one of its articles.
explanation.walkthrough: The magazine is a gun's ammunition holder, not a periodical, so the article is a round loaded into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is an item loaded into a firearm's magazine, the store of rounds feeding the gun.

clue.text: Shop lacking cover has rent put up, accommodating supplier

indicators.note: lacking cover means the outside letters of the word shop are stripped away
put up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A shop without a roof has had its rent raised while it supplies goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns LET into TEL. The definition plays on 'accommodating': a business that supplies accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a business whose trade is providing rooms, so it supplies accommodation to guests.

clue.text: Geordie gets a break, being the most close

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Tyneside in North East England, abbreviated NE
a rest is a break from work

explanation.surface: A Newcastle man is given time off, being the closest at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a person from Newcastle upon Tyne in North East England.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest is the superlative of near, meaning closest in distance.

clue.text: Profitable jobs for students with no Latin

indicators.note: with no means the following item is taken out of the students' word

parts.note: learners are people studying or being taught

explanation.surface: Lucrative work is available for students who have not taken Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Earners in British slang are money-makers, so a nice little earner is a lucrative sideline or job.

clue.text: Under a strain to retain head of state

annotationWithheld.why: Under a strain to retain head of state: TSAR is RAST hidden in 'Under a strain' read backwards, but 'retain' must signal both the hiding and the reversal (the blog reads it as 'keep back'), one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Under a strain to retain head of state

clue.text: Second minor argument is awkward

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A brief second squabble makes for an uncomfortable atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff manners are formal and uneasy, so stiff serves as a synonym for awkward.

clue.text: A good deal of embarrassment shown by the king

indicators.note: shown by places the king's word ahead of the embarrassment word

parts.note: royal means belonging to the king
a flush is a reddening of the face from embarrassment

explanation.surface: The monarch blushes deeply at something mortifying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' is a hand dealt at poker, not an amount or a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker a royal flush, ace to ten in one suit, is the best hand that can be dealt.

clue.text: Precious little weight — a ton attached to vehicle

indicators.note: attached to places the vehicle word first with the rest stuck on after it

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: A heavy load is hitched to a car, yet it weighs almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious' points to gemstones: the weight is the tiny unit for weighing jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat is a small unit of weight, 200 milligrams, used for gemstones and precious metals.

clue.text: A couple of Mary's rhymes are a bit vague

definitions.meaning: two words that rhyme with the name Mary, side by side

explanation.surface: Two nursery verses about Mary turn out to be rather woolly.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy-fairy describes ideas that are fanciful and unrealistic, so it is an idiom for vague.

clue.text: Amount of water required for walk

parts.note: water is a fluid, abbreviated FL as in a measure of liquid
an ounce is an amount, a unit of measure

explanation.surface: Someone needs a certain quantity of water before setting off on a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as FL OUNCE, the fluid ounce, a liquid measure of a twentieth of a British pint.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounce is to walk off in an exaggerated, impatient or huffy way.

clue.text: Spell 'Assuage'

definitions.meaning: to take over a duty from someone so they can rest, taking a spell at it
to ease or lessen pain or distress

explanation.definitionFit: Relieve means both to take over a shift from a worker and to ease a pain.

clue.text: Lights not working inside of hall

parts.note: a machine that is off is not working

indicators.note: inside of means only the inner letters of the word hall are used

explanation.surface: The lamps in the hallway have failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights' are not lamps but animal lungs, sold as butcher's meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights are the lungs of slaughtered animals, a kind of offal eaten or fed to pets.

clue.text: The end of the world means papacy lose ground

indicators.note: lose ground suggests the letters of the two words fall apart and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Armageddon will arrive if the Pope's office goes into decline.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocalypse, from the Book of Revelation, is the prophesied destruction at the world's end.

clue.text: Actors follow school production for internet transmission

indicators.note: follow puts the actors' word after the school word

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
the cast is the group of actors in a show

explanation.surface: Performers stage a school play to be streamed online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a group of whales, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A podcast is an audio programme made to be downloaded or streamed over the internet.

clue.text: What may follow shopping scared a revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary hints that the letters turn over into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebel was frightened while out shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes a phrase: shopping arcades.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcades are covered rows of shops, and shopping arcades is a familiar phrase.

clue.text: Clock put back by star

parts.note: the Sun is a star

indicators.note: back means the word for put is read in reverse

parts.note: laid means put down

explanation.surface: A timepiece is set back an hour according to the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundial tells the time from a shadow cast by the sun, an early kind of clock.

clue.text: Sisters welcome assignation to support island from floods

indicators.note: to support in a down clue places the island letter on top, with the rest beneath it
welcome means the sisters' word takes in the assignation word

parts.note: nuns are religious sisters
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: Nuns greet a romantic meeting held on an isle, from the floodwaters.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue a piece that supports another sits under it, so I comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Inundates means floods or swamps, as water covers land.

clue.text: Style of hair men ignore

parts.note: a crew is the men working a ship
to cut someone is to snub or ignore them

explanation.surface: A hairstyle that men don't bother with.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short, bristly haircut, a style once typical of the military.

clue.text: Around the third of July arrange a quiet drink

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters wrap about the July letter
arrange signals putting the letters of the two words in a new order
the third of picks the letter in third position

explanation.surface: Around early July, organise a quiet drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrange' rearranges A and QUIET to give TEQUIA, which goes 'Around' L, the third letter of July.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila is a Mexican spirit made from agave, a strong alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Cheeky lads pinch the woman's little darlings

indicators.note: pinch means the lads' word grips the woman's word inside it

parts.note: cubs are young, cheeky boys, as in Cub Scouts
her means belonging to the woman

explanation.surface: Naughty boys steal from a lady her beloved children.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubs are angelic infants, and the word is used for sweet little children or darlings.

clue.text: Converted, caught and executed

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
hanged means put to death by hanging

explanation.surface: A criminal was arrested and put to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Converted means altered from one form to another, so changed is a synonym.

clue.text: Island seized by fat landowner

indicators.note: seized by means the island letter is gripped inside the fat word

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: An island is grabbed by an overweight estate holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish landowner, the owner of an estate.

clue.text: Building where soldier's put up ladies

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the soldier word is read upwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier; the 's means 'is'
the ladies is a women's lavatory, a loo

explanation.surface: A soldier is billeted where the women's toilets are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns GI into IG. The ladies is British for a women's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped Inuit dwelling built of snow blocks, a kind of building.

clue.text: Put down question and answer (Slough)

parts.note: to slough a skin is to shed it

explanation.surface: A quiz has been suppressed in the Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the town west of London, but it is the verb for casting off skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To quash a rebellion is to put it down, suppress it.

clue.text: Pull hard, not quite attaining paradise

indicators.note: not quite attaining means the word for paradise stops short of its final letter

parts.note: heaven is paradise

explanation.surface: Someone tugs with all their might, yet falls short of bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to haul or lift something with great effort.

clue.text: Perfect husband described in this way

indicators.note: described in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A model spouse is portrayed like this.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus means in this manner, so it is a synonym of this way.

clue.text: Brushing up language, one never gets to start

parts.note: Polish is the language of Poland
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to start takes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Improving a foreign tongue that someone never gets to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Polishing a skill means refining it, which is the idiom brushing up.

clue.text: An urge for a letter

parts.note: an itch is a strong urge or longing

explanation.surface: A craving to write to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelt-out name of a letter of the alphabet, the eighth.

clue.text: Love affair so ends at last, finding God

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A romance ends finally with the discovery of a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love.

clue.text: Prison officers struggle with shifts

parts.note: a war is a struggle or conflict
a shift is a simple straight dress

explanation.surface: Jail staff wrestle with changes in their working hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' are not work rotas but loose, simple dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Wardresses are female prison guards, the women's equivalent of warders.
